actual_step.title: Use numpy.asarray when copying the input is allowed
actual_step.explanation: NumPy 2 makes array(..., copy=False) reject inputs that require a copy; the observed numpy.array call raises that specific error. This environment has numpy 2.2.6. Replace numpy.array(values, copy=False, ...) with numpy.asarray(values, ...), keeping the dtype and other needed options. If the program truly requires zero copying, keep that requirement and provide a compatible array buffer instead. Do not change the expected values. The compatibility diagnosis is a hypothesis supported by this symptom and version context; verify the result with the original test suite.
rules: H10: A specific documented behavior change fits the observed failure and the project's version context. Confirm the intended behavior by applying the narrow remedy and rerunning unchanged tests.

actual_step.title: Give the optional model field an explicit None default
actual_step.explanation: Pydantic V2 requires an Optional field when its declaration has no default. The actual missing field is nullable without a default and the supplied input has no unknown field names. This environment has pydantic 2.11.9. Locate the missing Optional field in the model declaration, and add = None if omitting that field is intended (for example email: Optional[str] = None). Keep other required fields and validation intact. Optional controls whether None is allowed; the explicit default controls omission. The compatibility diagnosis is a hypothesis supported by this symptom and version context; verify the result with the original test suite.

actual_step.explanation: NumPy 2 treats a non-1D b as matrices in linalg.solve. The captured a and b shapes fit the previous batched-vector contract but the call now reports a core-dimension mismatch. This environment has numpy 2.2.6. For the observed batched-vector call, replace numpy.linalg.solve(a, b) with numpy.linalg.solve(a, b[..., None])[..., 0]. Preserve a, b and the expected numeric result; the extra dimension makes the vector interpretation explicit.
